title: Identification of the normalized Cartesian proper/open comparison with its specified mate
statement: Let A be a commutative ring. Work with ordinary constant-A module sheaves on the small etale sites of arbitrary schemes and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For a fixed Cartesian square Q with top open immersion k:U→V, bottom open immersion i:W→Z and proper vertical maps r:U→W and p:V→Z, fix natural isomorphisms theta_Q:r_*⋙i_! ≅ k_!⋙p_* and Gamma_Q:Rr_*⋙Di_! ≅ Dk_!⋙Rp_*. Assume the support normalization: theta_Q,F followed by p_*(k_!F→k_*F) and the direct-image compositor equals i_!r_*F→i_*r_*F followed by the compositor into (ir)_*F=(pk)_*F [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition]. Assume also right-derived-unit normalization. For every homotopy object X on U, Di_!(eta_r,X) followed by Gamma_Q at Qh(X) equals the exact factorization for i_!, followed by Qh of theta_Q on X, the derived unit for p_* at k_!X, and Rp_* of the inverse exact factorization for k_!. Here eta denotes the right-derived unit and all exact factorizations are the canonical termwise localization isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived, lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. For every Cartesian Q the natural transformation Gamma_Q is exactly the mate, along inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions for r and p, of the inverse of the canonical termwise open-extension base-change isomorphism. Equivalently it is the unit for p, followed by Rp_* of the inverse open base-change comparison at Rr_*K, then Rp_*Dk_! of the counit for r. This is the specified map of [lem-sf-etale-proper-open-tensor-square], not merely an unspecified isomorphism. No Noetherianity or boundedness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: The normalized ordinary sheaf comparison is the adjunction mate of the inverse open base-change map: compose with the monic inclusion into the ordinary direct image, use open base-change compatibility with that inclusion, and the adjunction triangle identities. The support equation gives equality after this inclusion. Right-derived transformation uniqueness then identifies the given Gamma with the derived mate, since the unit normalization and the derived-mate unit formula agree. The descended open base-change isomorphism is exactly the one in the specified exchange.

theorem etaleProperOpenCartesianNormalization
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A]
    {U V W Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (k : U ⟶ V) (r : U ⟶ W) (p : V ⟶ Z) (i : W ⟶ Z)
    [IsOpenImmersion k] [IsOpenImmersion i] [IsProper r] [IsProper p]
    (sq : IsPullback r k i p)
    (θ : (r)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A] ⋙ (i)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A] ≅
      (k)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A] ⋙ (p)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A])
    (hθ : ∀ F : Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A), θ.hom.app F ≫
            (p)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A].map
              ((openImmersionLowerShriekToLowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) k).app F) ≫
            (lowerStarComp.{u + 2, u} (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) k p).hom.app F =
          (openImmersionLowerShriekToLowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) i).app
              ((r)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A].obj F) ≫
            (lowerStarComp.{u + 2, u} (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) r i
              (k ≫ p) sq.toCommSq.flip.w).hom.app F)
    (Γ : R((r)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]) ⋙ D((i)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]) ≅
      D((k)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]) ⋙ R((p)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]))
    (hΓ : ProperOpenUnitNormalized
      (r)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A] (p)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]
      (k)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A] (i)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A] θ.hom Γ.hom) :
    Γ.hom = openImmersionLowerShriekLowerStarExchange (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) sq
